Apple (AAPL)
stock is at an interesting point right now. It has strong momentum, and if you bet on it, you are betting on a company with strong margin, good cash flow, low-debt capital structure, and good tailwinds. But is that enough? Why Bet On AAPL Now? The primary driver for equity appreciation is the ongoing mix shift toward the high-margin services business. By monetizing its growing installed base of over 2.5 billion active devices, Apple is transforming its earnings profile from one dependent on cyclical hardware sales to a more predictable, high-quality, recurring revenue stream, which justifies a premium valuation. Services revenue grew 16% YoY in Q2 FY2026 to an all-time record high of $31 billion. The installed base of active devices now exceeds 2.5 billion, providing a large and growing base for monetization. Services Gross Margin stood at 74.2%.

[AAPL] TTM gross margin reached 47.9%, up from 46.2% in FY 2024 and 38.2% back in FY 2019, driven by the rising Services mix. Operating margin now sits at 32.6%, and the company throws off $129.2 billion in free cash flow on a TTM basis. That FCF easily covers the $7.7 billion in dividends and $37.0 billion in buybacks Apple executed in the first half of FY 2026. The balance sheet is fortress-grade. Apple holds $146.6 billion in cash and marketable securities against $82.7 billion in term debt. Net cash position is positive and growing. Valuation
Source: Seeking Alpha
Apple trades at a premium to nearly every peer on this list, with the exception of
Seagate Technology (STX)
. On forward P/E, Apple sits at 33.5x versus
Sandisk (SNDK)
at 24.2x,
Western Digital (WDC)
at 29.7x, and
Dell Technologies (DELL)
at just 22.2x. Price-to-cash-flow tells a similar story. Apple commands 30.7x, well above Dell’s 14.4x but cheaper than WDC and STX. The market is paying up for Apple’s Services mix, capital returns, and brand moat. Whether that’s justified is the central question. Growth
Source: Seeking Alpha
Here’s where the premium gets harder to defend. Apple’s 12.8% YoY revenue growth trails SNDK’s 82.8% surge, WDC’s 32.0%, and STX’s 28.9%. Forward revenue growth of 9.6% is the weakest in the group except WDC. Yet Apple’s three-year revenue CAGR of 5.4% beats WDC and SNDK, both of whom posted negative numbers over that stretch. The hardware peers are riding an AI-driven storage upcycle. Apple is the steadier compounder. Profitability
Source: Seeking Alpha
This is Apple’s home turf. Apple’s 47.9% gross margin trails only SNDK’s 56.0%. EBITDA margin of 35.4% beats every peer except SNDK. Levered FCF margin of 22.4% leads the group. Return on common equity of 141.5% dwarfs everyone except STX, which benefits from a tiny equity base. Most striking: Apple generated $140.2 billion in cash from operations on a TTM basis. The next closest, Dell, did $11.2 billion. Continued…
Our Opinion 7/10
Apple’s quarter was a genuine surprise to the upside, and the company’s cash generation remains in a league of its own. The dividend hike and fresh $100 billion buyback give investors a tangible return floor. But the stock isn’t cheap. At 33.5x forward earnings with sub-10% forward revenue growth, you’re paying a quality premium that leaves little room for an iPhone stumble or a tariff escalation. For long-term holders, Apple stays a core position.

[AAPL] Wearables also returned to growth, helped by new health features and improved battery life. While macro softness in China remained a headwind, investors responded positively to evidence of content and advertising revenue re-acceleration within the Services segment, which delivered double-digit growth. We continue to view Apple as one of the world’s most resilient and profitable businesses, supported by a massive installed base, ecosystem lock-in, and growing high-margin revenue streams. As Apple Intelligence features proliferate across devices, we expect multi-year upgrades, improved monetization, and expanded recurring revenue. With strong cash generation, ongoing share repurchases, and disciplined capital allocation, Apple remains a compelling long- term investment.”

records.query: NVIDIA 最近跟 IREN 之間有什麼合作的新聞？
records.answer:
NVIDIA 最近與 IREN（前身為 Iris Energy）簽訂了一項五年的 AI Cloud 合約，金額為 34 億美元，同時 NVIDIA 也對 IREN 進行了最高 21 億美元的投資，以支持其全球 AI 基礎設施部署 [NVDA_News_20260508_01.txt, chunk #1] [NVDA_News_20260508_02.txt, chunk #0]。

以下是雙方合作的具體細節：

**1. 34 億美元 AI Cloud 合約**
IREN 與 NVIDIA 簽訂了一項為期五年、價值 34 億美元的 AI Cloud 合約，部署空冷式 Blackwell GPU [NVDA_News_20260508_02.txt, chunk #0]。該合約預計在 Childress 現有數據中心的 60 MW 容量內進行部署，目標在 2027 年初開始放量 [NVDA_News_20260508_02.txt, chunk #0]。IREN 財務長表示，該 34 億美元合約中大約有 7 億美元的年經常性收入（ARR），支援部署於 Childress 60 MW 空冷容量中的 Blackwell GPU [NVDA_News_20260508_01.txt, chunk #2]。

黃仁勳向 Bloomberg Television 表示，H200 晶片已獲得向中國銷售的許可（"H200s are licensed to sell to China"），但目前沒有跡象顯示中國科技企業正在購買 [NVDA_News_20260519_03.txt, chunk #0]。黃仁勳在接受 Bloomberg Television 採訪時表示，他並未與北京高層官員討論 H200 的銷售事宜 [NVDA_News_20260519_03.txt, chunk #0]。

**中國政府需決定市場開放程度**
黃仁勳指出，「但中國政府必須決定他們想保護多少本地市場」，並補充說「我的感覺是，隨著時間推移，市場會開放」[NVDA_News_20260519_03.txt, chunk #1]。中國國家主席習近平向美國企業代表團表示，中國將向世界「進一步開放」[NVDA_News_20260519_03.txt, chunk #1]。

**川普與習近平達成的協議**
川普表示他已於去年12月與習近平達成協議，放寬對 H200 晶片的限制，但部分美國國會議員警告此舉可能幫助中國軍方 [NVDA_News_20260519_03.txt, chunk #1]。

**最高階產品仍被禁止銷售中國**
NVIDIA 最頂級的產品線——Blackwell 以及即將推出的 Rubin 系列——仍被禁止向中國銷售 [NVDA_News_20260519_03.txt, chunk #1]。

**中國聚焦發展自有 AI 處理器**
投資人原本希望習近平能允許 NVIDIA 向中國進口更多晶片，但川普向記者表示，中國反而正專注於發展自己的 AI 處理器 [NVDA_News_20260519_01.txt, chunk #1]。

**背景：川普訪中與AI競爭**
黃仁勳上週隨美國總統川普出訪中國，川普與習近平進行了會面；兩大強國正處於激烈的 AI 競爭之中 [NVDA_News_20260519_03.txt, chunk #0]。

records.answer:
NVIDIA 在財報前面臨的最主要市場焦點是 AI 晶片領域日益激烈的競爭以及中國市場的困境 [NVDA_News_20260519_01.txt, chunk #4]。

**競爭壓力來源：**

NVIDIA 在 AI 晶片領域面臨多方競爭。Cerebras（CBRS）於上週四舉行了 IPO，股價攀升 68%，該公司銷售一種與 NVIDIA 不同的 AI 處理器，並聲稱提供更快的整體效能速度 [NVDA_News_20260519_01.txt, chunk #4]。AMD 也構成競爭威脅，計劃於今年稍後推出競爭性的機架級伺服器系統 [NVDA_News_20260519_01.txt, chunk #4]。此外，NVIDIA 的客戶本身也成為競爭者——Amazon（AMZN）和 Google（GOOG/GOOGL）正將其自研 AI 晶片提供給第三方客戶，其中 Amazon 在最新財報中宣布其晶片業務年營收運行率已超過 200 億美元，且以三位數百分比年增長 [NVDA_News_20260519_01.txt, chunk #4]。

NVIDIA 的 10-K 申報文件進一步列出了更廣泛的競爭對手名單，包括 AMD、華為和 Intel 等離散 GPU 及加速運算解決方案供應商；阿里巴巴、Alphabet、Amazon、百度、華為和 Microsoft 等大型雲端服務公司內部團隊設計的硬體與軟體解決方案；以及 Tesla 等公司內部設計的 SoC 產品 [NVDA_10K_2026.html, chunk #31]。NVIDIA 表示預期競爭將日益加劇，部分競爭對手可能擁有比 NVIDIA 更強大的行銷、財務、分銷和製造資源 [NVDA_10K_2026.html, chunk #31]。

**中國市場困境：**

新聞報導指出，除了競爭加劇外，NVIDIA 同時面臨「中國困境」（China woes），這些問題被列為財報前市場關注的焦點之一 [NVDA_News_20260519_01.txt, chunk #4]。

**NVIDIA 的競爭優勢與平台策略：**

面對競爭，NVIDIA 的核心優勢在於其深度且廣泛的軟體堆疊，包括基礎的 CUDA 開發平台以及數百個特定領域的軟體庫、框架、演算法、SDK 和 API [NVDA_10K_2026.html, chunk #20]。NVIDIA 採取平台策略，整合硬體、系統、軟體、演算法、函式庫、AI 模型、訓練資料集和服務，以統一的底層可程式架構支援多個十億美元級別的終端市場 [NVDA_10K_2026.html, chunk #20]。自成立以來，NVIDIA 已投入超過 767 億美元於研發 [NVDA_10K_2026.html, chunk #20]。在 Blackwell 架構中，NVIDIA 採取極致的協同設計，將基礎設施的晶片、網路、系統、軟體和演算法進行整體架構與最佳化，數十萬顆 GPU 可互聯運作為一台巨型電腦 [NVDA_10K_2026.html, chunk #20]。

records.query: 微軟最近在 AI 策略上有什麼新消息，分析師怎麼看？
records.answer:
微軟最近在 AI 策略上的最大動作是推出七款自建 AI 模型，聚焦微調與成本優化，顯示公司正降低對前沿實驗室的依賴，分析師對此持正面看法——TD Cowen 在 6 月 4 日重申買入評級並給出 540 美元目標價 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。

以下是各個面向的具體細節：

**AI 策略轉型與自建模型**
微軟在 Build 2026 大會上展示了其 AI 平台的進展，並重申了幫助用戶部署 AI 代理的計畫，同時正在打造自己的 OpenClaw 版本 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。七款全新自建模型標誌著微軟 AI 開發策略的轉變，公司已將大量 GPU 算力分配給內部研發團隊，以支撐其 AI 產品組合的新階段佈局 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。

**分析師觀點**
TD Cowen 於 2026 年 6 月 4 日重申對微軟的買入評級，設定 540 美元目標價，理由是微軟透過自建模型強化了其 AI 策略 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。分析師將微軟列為最佳「永久持有」股票之一 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。

**財務表現與 AI 投資影響**
在 2025 財年（截至 2025 年），微軟總營收達 2,817.24 億美元，較 2024 財年的 2,451.22 億美元增長 15%；營業收入為 1,285.28 億美元，同比增長 17% [MSFT_10K_2025.html, chunk #143]。其中，Intelligent Cloud 營收增長 21% 至 1,062.65 億美元，Azure 及其他雲服務營收增長 34% [MSFT_10K_2025.html, chunk #143]。不過，Microsoft Cloud 毛利率下降至 69%，主因是擴展 AI 基礎設施的成本影響，部分被 Azure 的效率提升所抵消 [MSFT_10K_2025.html, chunk #143]。營業支出增加 38 億美元（增幅 6%），主要受雲端與 AI 工程投資以及遊戲業務（含動視暴雪收購影響）驅動 [MSFT_10K_2025.html, chunk #143]。

**風險因素**
微軟在 10-Q 中指出，美國關稅政策波動、AI 出口管制政策變化（包括已撤銷的 AI Diffusion Rule 的潛在替代方案），以及擴大的出口許可條件，可能對微軟的業務、策略和營運產生不利影響，並可能推升營運成本、造成產品供應連續性的不確定性 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #81]。此外，網路安全相關的立法與監管行動也可能增加產品開發與安全成本 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #81]。

**生態系互動**
微軟前全球策略總監 Michele Fisher 於 6 月 8 日離職加入 Rezolve AI 擔任行銷長，顯示微軟 AI 領域人才在業界受到青睞 [MSFT_News_20260612_02.txt, chunk #0]。此外，長期深耕微軟生態系的 AvePoint 執行長指出，微軟 Office Cloud 約有 4 至 5 億用戶席位，而 Copilot 滲透率僅約 5%，顯示微軟 AI 產品仍有大幅成長空間 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #2]。AvePoint 同時正在向 Google、Salesforce、AWS 等多雲生態擴展，預期非微軟營收佔比將從目前不到 10% 提升至 30% 以上 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #2]。

records.query: 有沒有 Microsoft 參與 AI 資安合作的新聞？
records.answer:
是的，參考資料中有多則與 Microsoft 生態系相關的 AI 資安與治理動態，但並非 Microsoft 本身直接從事 AI 資安合作，而是 Microsoft 生態系內的合作夥伴在 AI 治理與資安領域有所佈局。

**AvePoint 的 AI 治理與資安產品線：** AvePoint 執行長 Tianyi Jiang 表示，該公司定位於 AI 基礎架構的資料層與模型層之間，協助企業管理資料資產、存取控制與保留政策 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #1]。該公司推出的 AgentPulse 工具已於第一季正式上市，可協助客戶發現跨雲環境（如 Gemini 和 Copilot）中運行的 AI 代理，控制其可存取的系統與資料，監控 token 消耗量，並在必要時關閉這些代理 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #2]。Jiang 指出，AI 代理的興起加劇了對「shadow AI」及 AI 相關風險的擔憂 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #1]。

**AvePoint 與 Microsoft 的關係：** Jiang 表示 AvePoint 在 Microsoft 生態系已營運超過 20 年，但並不依賴 Microsoft 作為經銷商，Microsoft 並不轉售 AvePoint 的產品 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #2]。AvePoint 協助客戶完成 Purview、E5 和 Copilot 等「最後一哩」的工作負載採用 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #2]。Jiang 指出，Microsoft Office Cloud 約有 4 至 5 億個使用者席位，而 AvePoint 覆蓋「數千萬」席位，尚未達到 1 億，仍有成長空間 [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #2]。他提到 E5 滲透率仍低於 20%，Copilot 滲透率約為 5% [MSFT_News_20260612_03.txt, chunk #2]。

**Microsoft 自身的 AI 策略動態：** TD Cowen 於 6 月 4 日重申對 Microsoft 的買入評級，設定 540 美元目標價，理由是 Microsoft 以七款自建模型展現其 AI 策略，專注於微調與成本優化 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。報導指出，此舉代表 Microsoft 在 AI 發展上減少對前沿實驗室（frontier labs）的依賴，並已將大量 GPU 算力分配給內部研發團隊 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。在 Build 2026 大會上，Microsoft 展示了 AI 平台進展，並重申協助客戶部署 AI 代理的計畫 [MSFT_News_20260612_01.txt, chunk #0]。

**Rezolve AI 聘用 Microsoft 資深人士：** Rezolve AI（RZLV）於 6 月 8 日宣布聘請曾任 Microsoft 全球策略總監的 Michele Fisher 擔任行銷長，以擴大其 AI 平台的商業版圖 [MSFT_News_20260612_02.txt, chunk #0]。不過此消息與 AI 資安的關聯性較為間接，主要涉及企業 AI 平台的商業化推展。

**補充說明：** 參考資料中未提及 Microsoft 本身與其他公司簽署專門的 AI 資安合作協議；上述內容主要圍繞 Microsoft 生態系合作夥伴（如 AvePoint）在 AI 治理與資安領域的產品佈局，以及 Microsoft 自身的 AI 模型策略。

records.answer:
Microsoft 最新一季（截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日的季度）整體營業利益成長了 $6.4 billion，增幅為 20%，主要由 Productivity and Business Processes 及 Intelligent Cloud 兩個部門帶動 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。

**各部門表現如下：**

- **Productivity and Business Processes**：營收成長由 Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud 帶動 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。
- **Intelligent Cloud**：營收成長由 Azure 驅動 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。
- **More Personal Computing**：營收下降，主因為 Devices 與 Gaming 的 hardware sales 較低，部分被 Search advertising 的成長所抵銷 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。

**其他財務細節：**

- 營收增加 $12.8 billion，增幅 18%，由 Microsoft Cloud 成長驅動 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。
- 銷貨成本增加 $4.9 billion，增幅 22%，由 Microsoft Cloud 成長帶動 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。
- 毛利增加 $7.9 billion，增幅 16%，各部門均有成長 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。
- 營業費用增加 $1.5 billion，增幅 9%，主要受研發運算能力、AI 人才及數據的持續投資所驅動 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。
- 總員工人數較上年同期下降 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。
- 營收、毛利及營業利益分別包含 3%、3% 及 4% 的有利匯率影響 [MSFT_10Q_202603.html, chunk #102]。

Xbox content and services revenue decreased 2% driven by a decline in first-party content, offset in part by growth in Xbox Game Pass and third-party content. •Search and news advertising revenue increased $726 million or 11%.

[MSFT 10-Q period 202512] Operating income increased $3.0 billion or 28%. •Cost of revenue increased $4.2 billion or 44% driven by growth in Azure. •Gross margin increased $3.2 billion or 20% driven by growth in Azure. Gross margin percentage decreased driven by the continued investments in AI infrastructure and sales mix shift to Azure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure. •Operating expenses increased $180 million or 3% driven by research and development investments in compute capacity and AI talent. Cost of revenue included an unfavorable foreign currency impact of 2%. More Personal Computing

Revenue decreased $401 million or 3%. •Windows and Devices revenue decreased slightly. Windows OEM and Devices revenue increased 1% driven by Windows OEM growth of 5% with continued benefit from Windows 10 end of support and inventory levels that remained elevated, offset in part by a decline in Devices. •Gaming revenue decreased $623 million or 9% driven by declines in Xbox hardware and Xbox content and services. Xbox hardware revenue decreased 32% driven by lower volume of consoles sold. Xbox content and services revenue decreased 5% on a prior year comparable that benefited from strong first-party content performance. •Search and news advertising revenue increased $254 million or 7%.

[MSFT 10-Q period 202603] These non-GAAP financial measures exclude net gains and losses from investments in OpenAI. Refer to the Non-GAAP Financial Measures section below for a reconciliation of our financial results reported in accordance with GAAP to non-GAAP financial results. Three Months Ended March 31, 2026 Compared with Three Months Ended March 31, 2025

Revenue increased $12.8 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure. Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. More Personal Computing revenue decreased with lower hardware sales across Devices and Gaming, offset in part by growth in Search advertising. Cost of revenue increased $4.9 billion or 22% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Gross margin increased $7.9 billion or 16% with growth across each of our segments. •Gross margin percentage decreased driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage, offset in part by efficiency gains across the Microsoft Cloud. •Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 66% driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. Operating expenses increased $1.5 billion or 9% primarily driven by continued investments in research and development compute capacity, AI talent, and data to support product development across the portfolio. Total company headcount declined year-over-year. Operating income increased $6.4 billion or 20% driven by growth in Productivity and Business Processes and Intelligent Cloud. Revenue, gross margin, and operating income included a favorable foreign currency impact of 3%, 3%, and 4%, respectively.

[MSFT 10-Q period 202512] Search and news advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 10% driven by higher search volume and continued benefit from third-party partnerships. Operating income decreased $114 million or 3%. •Cost of revenue decreased $523 million or 8% driven by lower hardware sales. •Gross margin increased $122 million or 2% driven by growth in Search and news advertising and Windows OEM, offset in part by Gaming. Gross margin percentage increased driven by sales mix shift to higher margin businesses. •Operating expenses increased $236 million or 6% driven by impairment charges in our Gaming business and research and development investments in compute capacity and AI talent. Six Months Ended December 31, 2025 Compared with Six Months Ended December 31, 2024

Productivity and Business Processes

Revenue increased $9.4 billion or 16%. •Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased $6.9 billion or 17%. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 17% with growth in revenue per user driven by Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 Copilot, and continued Microsoft 365 Commercial seat growth. Microsoft 365 Commercial products revenue grew 15% driven by Windows Commercial on-premises components of Microsoft 365 suite sales, as well as an increase in Office 2024 transactional purchasing. •Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased $961 million or 27%. Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue grew 27% driven by growth in revenue per user and continued growth in Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers. •LinkedIn revenue increased $917 million or 10% driven by growth in Marketing Solutions. •Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased $578 million or 15% driven by growth in Dynamics 365. Dynamics 365 revenue grew 19% with growth across all workloads. Operating income increased $7.6 billion or 23%. •Cost of revenue increased $968 million or 9% driven by growth in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. •Gross margin increased $8.4 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. Gross margin percentage increased driven by efficiency gains in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud even with the impact of investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage. •Operating expenses increased $809 million or 6% driven by research and development investments in compute capacity and AI talent, as well as higher advertising expenses. Revenue, gross margin, and operating income included a favorable foreign currency impact of 2%, 3%, and 3%, respectively. Intelligent Cloud

Revenue increased $14.2 billion or 29%. •Server products and cloud services revenue increased $13.9 billion or 30% driven by Azure and other cloud services. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 40% driven by demand for our portfolio of services with continued growth across all workloads. Server products revenue increased 2% driven by higher transactional purchasing and demand for our hybrid solutions, with benefit from the launch of SQL Server 2025. •Enterprise and partner services revenue increased $240 million or 6% driven by growth in Enterprise Support Services.

It sells its products through OEMs, distributors, and resellers; and online and retail stores.
